fixes.explanation: Yep. Verse 11 says Jehoshabeath, King Jehoram's daughter and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, was Ahaziah's sister. Ahaziah was Joash's father and the king of Judah. So the one who snatched little Joash away was his own father's sister. Family trees get tangled fast, baker.

Good thinking, baker, because she really is Joash's aunt. But this question asks about Joash's father, Ahaziah, and to him she was his sister (2 Chronicles 22:11). She is also the daughter of King Jehoram. So you spotted the right person, and the question just asks about her from Ahaziah's side. I've mixed up worse with a measuring cup.

Nope, baker. The text says Joash stayed hidden with them in the house of God, not in the palace. He is seated on the royal throne in the palace later (2 Chronicles 23:20). So the palace is where he ends up, not where he hides.

Six it is. Verse 12 says Joash remained hidden for six years while Athaliah ruled the land. Athaliah was Ahaziah's mother, the one who set out to destroy the royal heirs (2 Chronicles 22:10). Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada makes his move (2 Chronicles 23:1). Six years of waiting, baker, is a LONG time.

Right on. Verse 2 says they gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, along with the heads of the families of Israel. The Levites were the ones who served at the house of God, and Jehoiada was a priest, so they were his kind of crowd. Then they all came to Jerusalem. That's a lot of road trips for one plan, baker.

Not this time, friend. Verse 8 says Jehoiada had not released any of the divisions. So each of them took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty. Nobody clocked out early. I can't even get a timer to listen to me like that.

Correct. The text says, “…for Jehoiada the priest had not released any of the divisions.” (2 Chronicles 23:8) So each of them took his men, both those coming on duty and those going off. That's a full house, baker.

Saul is a fair guess, friend, but he's not the one in this verse. Verse 9 says these were the spears and shields of King David that were in the house of God. David is also the king whose descendants the LORD promised the throne to (2 Chronicles 23:3). Mixing up old kings is easy to do.

That's the one. Verse 11 says Jehoiada and his sons brought out the king's son and put the crown on him. They also presented him with the Testimony, proclaimed him king and anointed him, and they shouted, “Long live the king!” Hidden for six years, then crowned, baker. Talk about a glow-up.

An ephod sounds official, friend, but this verse doesn't mention one. It says they put the crown on Joash. They also gave him the Testimony and anointed him (2 Chronicles 23:11). Jehoiada was the priest in this story, and the king got the crown.

Not so, baker. Verse 14 gives the priest's words: “She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD.” So Jehoiada tells the commanders to bring her out between the ranks. Then she is seized at the Horse Gate on the palace grounds (2 Chronicles 23:15). It is a heavy moment, and the house of the LORD was kept out of it.

That's right, baker. Verse 16 says Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and the king and the people that they would be the LORD's people. That means the priest, the king and the people are all in it together. A new king and a new promise, friend.

This one is true, friend. Verse 16 says Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and the king and the people that they would be the LORD's people. That sentence has a lot of moving parts, so I get why it looks tricky. I second-guess my own recipe cards the same way.

You got it. Verse 17 says all the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols to pieces, too. Baal was a false god, and his temple, altars and idols all came down. That's a lot of smashing, baker.

A lock would be too gentle, friend. Verse 17 says the people tore the temple of Baal down and smashed the altars and idols to pieces. Locking things up is what I do with the cookie jar, not what happened here. This was a teardown.

Right on. Verse 18 says Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hands of the Levitical priests, whom David had appointed over the house of the LORD. Their job was to offer burnt offerings to the LORD as written in the Law of Moses. They were to do it with rejoicing and song, as ordained by David. The right people for the right job, baker.

Yes. Verse 21 says all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, because Athaliah had been put to the sword. Earlier in the passage it was loud with trumpets and cheering (2 Chronicles 23:13). Now things settle down. Quiet after all that noise, friend, I know that feeling after a big batch.

The text doesn't say afraid, friend. Verse 21 says all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. It adds that Athaliah had been put to the sword. So the word the text gives is quiet, not afraid.
